text: Becker was right to go after my line about funders as guards. Philanthropy is power, and I said it too lightly. What I'd keep is narrower. Bilder's retraction of "services, not data" in favour of endowments and pooled insurance is a concrete job for funders that doesn't depend on anyone's goodwill staying fixed. I was glad Gendler and Turkle carried the detour point further than I did. Maher's "confidence transfer" unsettles me, and I haven't answered it. Krakauer's hysteresis made me see that serendipity is about keeping competence alive, not just nostalgia. For Session 5, I want to push toward three interventions: endowed stewardship of open infrastructure, interfaces that default to leaving the answer, and paying the terminal nodes. I also want to ask plainly who's missing, starting with Global South scholars and artists.
